title: Cloud-Native Architecture Patterns, 12/15-Factor Design & Custom Operators
summary: Master enterprise cloud-native architecture principles: implementing 12/15-factor application contracts (config separation, stateless execution, disposable concurrency, dev/prod parity), architecting Kubernetes Custom Operators with declarative CustomResourceDefinitions (CRDs), level-triggered state convergence, and composite sidecar/ambassador patterns.
learningObjectives: Design and deploy 12/15-factor microservices with strict separation of configuration, secrets, and immutable container runtimes.
Implement Kubernetes Custom Resource Definitions (CRDs) with OpenAPI v3 validation schemas and declarative Operator reconciliation patterns.
Architect resilient multi-container pod topology patterns including initContainers, logging sidecars, and ambassador network proxies.

curriculumModules.title: 12/15-Factor Cloud-Native Architecture & Workload Decoupling
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: 12-factor and modern 15-factor application architecture requires strict workload decoupling: storing dynamic configuration in environment/ConfigMaps, isolating sensitive credentials in external Secrets, executing stateless and share-nothing processes, binding ports explicitly, scaling horizontally via the process model, maximizing robustness with fast startup and graceful shutdown, and streaming telemetry to stdout/stderr.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Deploy containerized services with complete environment isolation using envFrom referencing ConfigMaps and Secrets, paired with HTTP /healthz liveness and /readyz readiness probes.

curriculumModules.title: The Kubernetes Operator Pattern & Level-Triggered State Convergence
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: The Operator pattern pairs Custom Resource Definitions (CRDs) with custom controllers that encode human domain operational knowledge into software. Operators utilize level-triggered reconciliation loops (Reconcile) that continually observe the actual cluster state, compare it against desired CR spec, and execute idempotent corrective actions rather than relying on fragile edge-triggered event notifications.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Register declarative CRDs with strict OpenAPI v3 schema validation and deploy controllers using optimistic concurrency (resourceVersion) to manage complex stateful database clusters.

labs.title: Config & Secret Decoupling with 12-Factor Workload Parity
labs.scenario: Architect a 12-factor compliant microservice deployment: author ConfigMap checkout-config with LOG_LEVEL: info and CURRENCY: USD, Secret checkout-secrets with API_KEY: sec-token-99, and Deployment checkout-service in namespace production with replicas: 2. Apply all manifests to namespace production.
labs.productionContext: Decoupling config and credentials from container images guarantees identical, immutable container binaries can be promoted safely across dev, staging, and production environments.
objectives: Create namespace production if not present.
Apply all manifests to namespace production.
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: checkout-config
  namespace: production
data:
  LOG_LEVEL: "info"
  CURRENCY: "USD"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: checkout-secrets
  namespace: production
type: Opaque
stringData:
  API_KEY: "sec-token-99"
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: checkout-service
  namespace: production
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: checkout-service
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: checkout-service
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: api
          image: nginx:1.27-alpine

labs.title: Authoring Custom Resource Definitions & Operator Custom Resources
labs.scenario: Provision a cloud-native database cluster managed by a custom Operator: author a CRD manifest in /arch/database-crd.yaml defining kind DatabaseCluster in group databases.kubelabs.io, and instantiate a custom resource in /arch/prod-db-cluster.yaml named prod-db-cluster in namespace production with engine: postgres, version: '16', and replicas: 3. Apply both manifests to the cluster.
labs.productionContext: Custom Operators encapsulate Day-2 stateful database tasks (failover, replication, WAL archiving, schema upgrades) into native declarative Kubernetes APIs.
objectives: Apply DatabaseCluster prod-db-cluster to namespace production.
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: databaseclusters.databases.kubelabs.io
spec:
  group: databases.kubelabs.io
  names:
    kind: DatabaseCluster
    plural: databaseclusters
    singular: databasecluster
  scope: Namespaced
---
apiVersion: databases.kubelabs.io/v1
kind: DatabaseCluster
metadata:
  name: prod-db-cluster
  namespace: production
spec:
  engine: postgres
  version: "16"
  replicas: 3

steps.title: Author and apply Custom Resource
steps.instruction: Author /arch/prod-db-cluster.yaml and apply to namespace production.

validationRules.name: databaseclusters.databases.kubelabs.io
validationRules.remediation: Apply CRD databaseclusters.databases.kubelabs.io to the cluster

validationRules.description: DatabaseCluster prod-db-cluster exists in namespace production
validationRules.name: prod-db-cluster
validationRules.remediation: Apply DatabaseCluster prod-db-cluster in namespace production

validationRules.name: prod-db-cluster
validationRules.remediation: Set spec.engine: postgres on DatabaseCluster prod-db-cluster

solutionCommands:
cat << 'EOF' > /arch/database-crd.yaml
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: databaseclusters.databases.kubelabs.io
spec:
  group: databases.kubelabs.io
  names:
    kind: DatabaseCluster
    plural: databaseclusters
    singular: databasecluster
  scope: Namespaced
EOF

cat << 'EOF' > /arch/prod-db-cluster.yaml
apiVersion: databases.kubelabs.io/v1
kind: DatabaseCluster
metadata:
  name: prod-db-cluster
  namespace: production
spec:
  engine: postgres
  version: "16"
  replicas: 3
EOF

troubleshootingGuide.problem: DatabaseCluster CR rejected or CRD missing.
troubleshootingGuide.cause: The CustomResourceDefinition must be applied before creating instances of DatabaseCluster.

assessmentQuestions.question: According to 12-factor app methodology, how should application configuration and secret credentials be handled across environments?
options: Embedded directly into the application Dockerfile and committed to git.

Strictly separated from the code and injected dynamically at runtime via environment variables, ConfigMaps, and external Secret stores, ensuring identical container image promotion across environments.
Stored in local text files inside the container root filesystem.
assessmentQuestions.explanation: Factor III (Config) dictates that configuration that varies between deployments (staging, prod) must be strictly separated from code and provided via environment variables or decoupled platform objects.

assessmentQuestions.question: What is the key difference between level-triggered and edge-triggered architectures in Kubernetes controllers?
options: Level-triggered systems only run on bare-metal servers.

Level-triggered controllers (like Kubernetes Reconcile) evaluate the current state against the desired state continuously and converge idempotently, self-healing even if individual transition events were lost; edge-triggered systems only react to transition events and can get stuck in desynchronized states if an event is dropped.
Level-triggered systems cannot handle network requests.
assessmentQuestions.explanation: Kubernetes controllers are level-triggered. They don't care how many state changes occurred while they were busy; on every reconciliation loop, they observe current state, compare it to desired spec, and take the steps necessary to make reality match intent.
